phases.name: Reassemble, road test & keep it running

parts.name: Radiator, hoses and fan (or cooling fins)

tasks.title: Identify your bike exactly
tasks.instructions: Find the VIN and the engine number, confirm the year and model from them, and note anything that isn't stock.
tasks.reason: The right manual, parts and recalls depend on the exact model and year.
tasks.expected: VIN, engine number, year and model recorded in Settings.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: VIN, engine number, year and model recorded in Settings.

tasks.title: Check for open recalls
tasks.instructions: Run the VIN through the NHTSA recall lookup (or your country's equivalent) and confirm with a dealer which recalls have been done.
tasks.reason: Recall repairs are free at a dealer and often cover the exact problem you'd otherwise pay to fix.
tasks.expected: Every open recall noted, or none found.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Every open recall noted, or none found.

tasks.title: Get the service manual
tasks.instructions: Get the factory service manual for your exact model and year, plus the owner's manual and a wiring diagram.
tasks.reason: Torque values, clearances, capacities and procedures in this course all come from the manual.
tasks.expected: Manual on hand and listed under Reference sources.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Manual on hand and listed under Reference sources.

tasks.title: Set up the workspace
tasks.instructions: Clear a space with good light, a stand or lift, bins for fasteners and a safe spot for fluids.
tasks.reason: A tidy space means fewer lost parts and fewer accidents.
tasks.tools: Stand or lift, shelves, bins, labels
tasks.expected: Bike secure on a stand; labeled bins and drain pans ready.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Bike secure on a stand; labeled bins and drain pans ready.

tasks.title: Set the budget
tasks.instructions: Set a budget in Settings with a cushion for surprises.
tasks.reason: Knowing the limit helps you decide between repair and replace as you go.
tasks.expected: Budget and safety cushion set in Settings.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Budget and safety cushion set in Settings.

tasks.title: Record the odometer and photograph everything
tasks.instructions: Record the odometer, then photograph the bike from every side and close up on damage, wiring routes and anything you'll need to put back.
tasks.reason: Before photos are your best reassembly guide and record the condition you started with.
tasks.expected: Odometer logged; before photos uploaded.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Odometer logged; before photos uploaded.

tasks.title: Check every fluid and look for leaks
tasks.instructions: Check the engine oil, coolant (if liquid-cooled), brake fluid and any final-drive oil for level and condition, and look for leaks.
tasks.reason: Low, milky or dark fluids and wet spots point straight at the jobs you need to do.
tasks.expected: Each fluid's level and condition recorded; leaks logged as problems.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Each fluid's level and condition recorded; leaks logged as problems.

tasks.title: Test compression
tasks.instructions: Do a compression test on every cylinder and compare the readings with the manual and with each other.
tasks.reason: Compression tells you if the rings and valves are healthy, which decides whether the engine needs opening up.
tasks.expected: Readings for every cylinder recorded in Measurements.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Readings for every cylinder recorded in Measurements.

tasks.title: Start it and listen
tasks.instructions: If the oil is good and the engine turns over freely, start it with fresh fuel and listen for knocks, rattles and rough running as it warms up.
tasks.reason: Noises and warning lights at start-up are early warnings of bigger problems.
tasks.expected: Start-up behavior, noises and warning lights recorded, or why it wouldn't start.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Start-up behavior, noises and warning lights recorded, or why it wouldn't start.

tasks.title: Short test ride, if it's safe
tasks.instructions: If the brakes work, the tires hold air and the steering is free, ride slowly around the block and note how it brakes, shifts and handles.
tasks.reason: A ride shows problems you can't find on the stand.
tasks.expected: Ride notes written, or ride skipped with the reason recorded.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Ride notes written, or ride skipped with the reason recorded.

tasks.title: Write the job list
tasks.instructions: Turn the inspection notes into a list of jobs, marking anything safety-related, and decide which parts of the course you'll do in full.
tasks.reason: A clear list keeps the project focused and drives the parts order.
tasks.expected: Problems logged with severity; job list agreed.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Problems logged with severity; job list agreed.

tasks.title: Look up part numbers on the diagrams
tasks.instructions: Use the factory parts diagrams for your year and model to find the part number for everything on the job list.
tasks.reason: The right part number is the only reliable way to order the right part.
tasks.expected: Part numbers entered on each part in Parts.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Part numbers entered on each part in Parts.

tasks.title: Price it and check the budget
tasks.instructions: Price each part from at least two shops including shipping and compare the total with the budget.
tasks.reason: Delivered prices vary more than you'd expect.
tasks.expected: Shopping list priced; budget forecast checked.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Shopping list priced; budget forecast checked.

tasks.title: Order the parts
tasks.instructions: Order the parts and supplies, recording order dates and tracking.
tasks.reason: Ordering everything at once avoids stopping halfway through a job.
tasks.expected: Every item ordered and tracked.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Every item ordered and tracked.

tasks.title: Remove the seat and side covers
tasks.instructions: Remove the seat and side covers, bagging and labeling each fastener.
tasks.reason: Access to the battery, fuses and wiring starts here.
tasks.expected: Seat and side covers off; fasteners bagged and labeled.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Seat and side covers off; fasteners bagged and labeled.

tasks.title: Disconnect and remove the battery
tasks.instructions: Disconnect the battery, negative first, and remove it for testing and charging.
tasks.reason: Working with the battery connected risks shorts and damaged electronics.
tasks.expected: Battery out and on a smart charger.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Battery out and on a smart charger.

tasks.title: Drain and remove the fuel tank
tasks.instructions: Drain the fuel into an approved can, disconnect the lines and any wiring, and remove the tank.
tasks.reason: The tank has to come off to reach the top of the engine, and a full tank is heavy and dangerous to handle.
tasks.expected: Tank off, drained and stored safely away from sparks.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Tank off, drained and stored safely away from sparks.

tasks.title: Wash and degrease
tasks.instructions: Clean the bike so you can see the frame, engine and wiring, protecting electrical parts and intakes.
tasks.reason: You can't inspect what you can't see.
tasks.expected: Bike clean; no water in connectors or intakes.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Bike clean; no water in connectors or intakes.

tasks.title: Inspect the frame and swingarm
tasks.instructions: Inspect the frame, subframe, mounts and swingarm for cracks, bends, rust and crash damage.
tasks.reason: A cracked or bent frame makes the bike unsafe, and it's far better to know now.
tasks.expected: Frame and swingarm checked; any damage logged.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Frame and swingarm checked; any damage logged.

tasks.title: Treat rust and protect bare metal
tasks.instructions: Remove surface rust, treat what's left, and protect bare metal so it doesn't come back.
tasks.reason: Rust spreads under paint and weakens thin parts.
tasks.expected: Rust treated and bare metal protected; deep rust on structural parts logged.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Rust treated and bare metal protected; deep rust on structural parts logged.

tasks.title: Inspect the wiring harness and connectors
tasks.instructions: Look over the harness for rubbed insulation, melted spots, old repairs and green corrosion in the connectors.
tasks.reason: Chafed wires and corroded connectors cause intermittent faults that are hard to find later.
tasks.expected: Harness checked; damage logged.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Harness checked; damage logged.

tasks.title: Test and charge the battery
tasks.instructions: Fully charge the battery and test it under load, or replace it if it's old or fails.
tasks.reason: A weak battery makes every other electrical test meaningless.
tasks.expected: Battery passes, or a new one is fitted.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Battery passes, or a new one is fitted.

tasks.title: Test the charging system
tasks.instructions: With a good battery fitted, measure charging voltage at the battery and test the stator or alternator and the regulator using the manual's procedure.
tasks.reason: This confirms the bike can keep its own battery charged.
tasks.expected: Readings recorded and compared with the manual's figures.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Readings recorded and compared with the manual's figures.

tasks.title: Clean the grounds, fuses and connectors
tasks.instructions: Clean and tighten the main ground points, check every fuse and fuse holder, and clean the main connectors.
tasks.reason: Bad grounds and corroded fuse holders cause most electrical faults on older bikes.
tasks.tools: Contact cleaner, fine sandpaper, dielectric grease
tasks.expected: Grounds clean and tight; fuses correct rating; connectors clean.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Grounds clean and tight; fuses correct rating; connectors clean.

tasks.title: Check the starter and ignition
tasks.instructions: Check that the starter spins the engine strongly, and that every cylinder gets a good spark. On older bikes, check the points and condenser.
tasks.reason: Weak cranking and weak spark are the usual reasons a restored bike won't start.
tasks.expected: Starter and spark checked on every cylinder.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Starter and spark checked on every cylinder.

tasks.title: Check lights, switches, horn and warning lamps
tasks.instructions: Test every light, the horn, every switch and every warning lamp, and confirm the brake light works from both the front and rear brakes.
tasks.reason: Riders need to see and be seen. This is a legal requirement as well as a safety one.
tasks.expected: Every light and switch works; brake light works from lever and pedal.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Every light and switch works; brake light works from lever and pedal.

tasks.title: Find out which fuel system it has
tasks.instructions: Check whether the bike has carburetors or fuel injection, and how many, and mark the steps below that don't apply as Cancelled.
tasks.reason: The fuel steps differ completely between carbs and injection.
tasks.expected: Fuel system type noted; steps that don't apply cancelled.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Fuel system type noted; steps that don't apply cancelled.

tasks.title: Clean the tank inside and check for rust
tasks.instructions: Look inside the tank for rust, scale and old fuel varnish, clean it out, and seal it if there are pinholes.
tasks.reason: Rust and varnish from the tank block filters, carbs and injectors again right after you clean them.
tasks.expected: Tank clean and dry inside; sealed if needed.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Tank clean and dry inside; sealed if needed.

tasks.title: Service the petcock or fuel pump, lines and filters
tasks.instructions: Rebuild or replace the petcock, check the fuel pump if it has one, replace the fuel lines and filters, and check the tank vent.
tasks.reason: Old fuel lines crack and leak, and a fuel leak is a fire risk.
tasks.expected: New lines and filters; petcock or pump working; no leaks.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: New lines and filters; petcock or pump working; no leaks.

tasks.title: Rebuild the carburetors
tasks.instructions: Remove the carburetors, rebuild them one at a time with new gaskets, O-rings and needle valves, clean every passage, and set the float height.
tasks.reason: Old fuel varnishes the jets and passages, and old rubber parts leak. Most bikes that have sat need this to run right.
tasks.tools: Carb rebuild kits, carb cleaner, small screwdrivers
tasks.expected: Carbs clean and rebuilt; float heights set to the manual's figure; jet sizes recorded.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Carbs clean and rebuilt; float heights set to the manual's figure; jet sizes recorded.

tasks.title: Check the fuel injection
tasks.instructions: Read any fault codes, clean the throttle plates, check the injector wiring and fuel pressure as the manual describes.
tasks.reason: Sticky throttle plates and fault codes cause rough running that cleaning and a reset often fix.
tasks.expected: No fault codes; throttle plates clean; idle steady.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: No fault codes; throttle plates clean; idle steady.

tasks.title: Air filter and intake boots
tasks.instructions: Replace or clean the air filter and check the intake boots between the carbs or throttle bodies and the engine for cracks.
tasks.reason: A cracked intake boot lets in air and makes the engine run lean and hot.
tasks.expected: New or clean filter; intake boots sealed and crack-free.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: New or clean filter; intake boots sealed and crack-free.

tasks.title: Synchronize the carbs or throttle bodies
tasks.instructions: On multi-cylinder bikes, synchronize the carbs or throttle bodies with vacuum gauges, then set the idle.
tasks.reason: Out-of-sync carbs or throttle bodies make the bike lumpy at low speed and harder to ride smoothly.
tasks.expected: Every cylinder balanced to the manual's figure; idle set.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Every cylinder balanced to the manual's figure; idle set.

tasks.title: Test the vacuum fuel petcock
tasks.instructions: Check the vacuum petcock opens only with vacuum and seals with the engine off, and replace its vacuum hose.
tasks.reason: A leaking vacuum petcock can flood the engine; a stuck one starves it.
tasks.expected: Petcock flows with vacuum and seals without; hose new.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Petcock flows with vacuum and seals without; hose new.

tasks.title: Change the oil and filter
tasks.instructions: Drain the warm oil, replace the filter and drain bolt washer, and refill with the type and amount the manual gives.
tasks.reason: Fresh oil is the cheapest engine protection there is, and old oil on a bike that sat may be full of water.
tasks.tools: Drain pan, filter wrench, torque wrench
tasks.expected: New oil and filter; level correct; no leaks.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: New oil and filter; level correct; no leaks.

tasks.title: Replace the spark plugs
tasks.instructions: Replace the spark plugs with the type the manual lists, gapped to spec.
tasks.reason: New plugs are cheap and rule out one cause of poor running.
tasks.tools: Plug socket, gap gauge, torque wrench
tasks.expected: New plugs fitted, gapped and torqued.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: New plugs fitted, gapped and torqued.

tasks.title: Check and adjust the valve clearances
tasks.instructions: With the engine cold, measure every valve clearance and adjust any that are out of spec using the manual's method.
tasks.reason: Tight valves burn, loose valves are noisy and wear the cams. It's one of the most skipped jobs.
tasks.expected: Every clearance recorded in Measurements and within spec.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Every clearance recorded in Measurements and within spec.

tasks.title: Service the cooling system
tasks.instructions: Liquid-cooled: replace the coolant, check the radiator, hoses, cap and fan. Air-cooled: clean the fins and check any oil cooler and lines.
tasks.reason: Overheating kills engines. Old coolant corrodes from the inside and old hoses split under pressure.
tasks.expected: Coolant fresh and bled, or fins and oil cooler clean; fan works.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Coolant fresh and bled, or fins and oil cooler clean; fan works.

tasks.title: Fix oil leaks and check the exhaust
tasks.instructions: Find and fix oil leaks at covers and seals, and check the exhaust for leaks, rust-through and loose mounts.
tasks.reason: Oil on the tires and brakes is dangerous, and exhaust leaks make the engine run badly.
tasks.expected: No oil leaks; exhaust sealed and mounts tight.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: No oil leaks; exhaust sealed and mounts tight.

tasks.title: Check tire age, tread and damage
tasks.instructions: Read the date code on both tires, measure the tread, and look for cracks, cuts, plugs and flat spots.
tasks.reason: Tires age out even with tread left. Old rubber is hard and slippery.
tasks.expected: Both tires pass, or replacements ordered.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Both tires pass, or replacements ordered.

tasks.title: Check the wheel bearings
tasks.instructions: With each wheel off the ground, check for play and rough rotation, and replace bearings and seals if needed.
tasks.reason: Worn bearings make the bike wander and can seize.
tasks.expected: No play; smooth rotation; seals intact.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: No play; smooth rotation; seals intact.

tasks.title: Inspect the rims and wheels
tasks.instructions: Check spoked wheels for loose or rusted spokes and runout, and cast wheels for cracks and bends.
tasks.reason: A cracked cast wheel or a wheel with loose spokes can fail on the road.
tasks.expected: Wheels true and sound, or sent to a wheel builder.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Wheels true and sound, or sent to a wheel builder.

tasks.title: Fit and balance new tires
tasks.instructions: Fit new tires in the size, load and speed rating the manual or tire placard gives, with new valves or tubes, and balance the wheels.
tasks.reason: The right tires correctly fitted and balanced are a basic safety item.
tasks.tools: Tire irons, balancer, or a shop
tasks.expected: Correct tires fitted, beads seated, balanced, pressures set.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Correct tires fitted, beads seated, balanced, pressures set.

tasks.title: Inspect the pads, shoes, discs and drums
tasks.instructions: Check pad or shoe thickness and disc or drum condition on both brakes against the manual's limits.
tasks.reason: Worn pads and thin discs are a straight safety issue.
tasks.expected: Pads or shoes and discs or drums within limits, or replacements ordered.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Pads or shoes and discs or drums within limits, or replacements ordered.

tasks.title: Rebuild or clean the calipers
tasks.instructions: Strip and clean the calipers, check the pistons for pitting, replace the seals if they're sticky, and fit new pads.
tasks.reason: Calipers on a bike that has sat usually stick. Sticky pistons drag and brake unevenly.
tasks.tools: Brake cleaner, caliper rebuild kits, torque wrench
tasks.expected: Pistons move smoothly; new seals and pads fitted; bolts torqued.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Pistons move smoothly; new seals and pads fitted; bolts torqued.

tasks.title: Service the master cylinders and hoses
tasks.instructions: Rebuild sticky master cylinders and replace any brake hoses that are cracked, bulging or very old.
tasks.reason: Old rubber hoses can swell inside and hold the brake on, or burst.
tasks.expected: Master cylinders working; hoses sound or replaced.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Master cylinders working; hoses sound or replaced.

tasks.title: Bleed in fresh brake fluid
tasks.instructions: Replace the brake fluid front and rear with the type on the reservoir cap, following the manual's order. On ABS bikes, follow the manual's ABS procedure.
tasks.reason: Brake fluid absorbs water and boils sooner. Air in the lines makes the brake spongy.
tasks.expected: Fresh fluid; firm lever and pedal; no leaks.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Fresh fluid; firm lever and pedal; no leaks.

tasks.title: Service the forks
tasks.instructions: Replace the fork oil and seals, check the tubes for pitting and bends, and set the oil level from the manual.
tasks.reason: Leaking seals put oil on the brakes; worn oil makes the front dive and bounce.
tasks.expected: Forks dry, oil at the right level, damping smooth.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Forks dry, oil at the right level, damping smooth.

tasks.title: Check the steering head bearings
tasks.instructions: With the front wheel off the ground, check for notchiness and play, and adjust, grease or replace the bearings.
tasks.reason: Worn steering bearings make the bike weave and feel vague, and a notchy one can make it hard to hold a line.
tasks.expected: Steering smooth with no play.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Steering smooth with no play.

tasks.title: Check the rear shocks and swingarm bearings
tasks.instructions: Check the shock or shocks for leaks and damping, the swingarm pivot and any linkage for play, and grease the bearings.
tasks.reason: Dry swingarm bearings wear fast and make the rear end vague; a blown shock bounces.
tasks.expected: Shocks dry and damping; no play at the pivot; bearings greased.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Shocks dry and damping; no play at the pivot; bearings greased.

tasks.title: Lube and adjust the control cables and levers
tasks.instructions: Lube the throttle and other cables, check they're not frayed, set throttle play, and check the levers, pedals and footpegs.
tasks.reason: A sticking throttle is one of the most dangerous faults a bike can have.
tasks.expected: Throttle snaps shut at both steering locks; cables lubed and adjusted; levers tight.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Throttle snaps shut at both steering locks; cables lubed and adjusted; levers tight.

tasks.title: Set the sag and suspension
tasks.instructions: Measure the sag with you on the bike and set the preload and any damping adjusters for your weight and load.
tasks.reason: The right sag makes the bike handle the way it was designed to.
tasks.expected: Sag and settings recorded.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Sag and settings recorded.

tasks.title: Plan the finish
tasks.instructions: Decide what gets refinished, what stays original, and who does each job, and record it.
tasks.reason: Planning the finish first stops you painting parts twice.
tasks.expected: A finish plan written for each part.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: A finish plan written for each part.

tasks.title: Repair the body panels and clips
tasks.instructions: Repair cracked panels and broken tabs, and replace missing clips and screws.
tasks.reason: Broken tabs rattle and crack further.
tasks.expected: Every panel fits snugly with all its clips and screws.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Every panel fits snugly with all its clips and screws.

tasks.title: Refinish the panels and refresh the seat
tasks.instructions: Paint the panels with a plastic primer system, and repair or recover the seat and replace the floor mats.
tasks.reason: Fresh panels and seat transform how a scooter looks.
tasks.expected: Panels painted; seat sound; mats new.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Panels painted; seat sound; mats new.

tasks.title: Reassemble the bike
tasks.instructions: Reassemble the bike in reverse order using your labeled bags and photos, routing cables and wiring the way they came out.
tasks.reason: Correct fasteners and routing keep the bike quiet, safe and reliable.
tasks.expected: Every part fitted; no leftover fasteners; cables and wiring routed as before.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Every part fitted; no leftover fasteners; cables and wiring routed as before.

tasks.title: Torque-check the critical fasteners
tasks.instructions: Check the axles, pinch bolts, caliper bolts, handlebar clamps, engine mounts and drain plugs against the manual's torque values.
tasks.reason: These are the fasteners that keep the wheels, brakes and engine attached.
tasks.expected: Each one checked, marked and initialed.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Each one checked, marked and initialed.

tasks.title: First start after the rebuild
tasks.instructions: Prime the oil system if the manual says to, check for fuel leaks, start the engine and watch for leaks, smoke and warning lights.
tasks.reason: The first start is when fuel leaks and wiring mistakes show up. Have a fire extinguisher ready.
tasks.expected: Engine starts and idles; no fuel or oil leaks; warning lights normal.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Engine starts and idles; no fuel or oil leaks; warning lights normal.

tasks.title: Test ride and recheck
tasks.instructions: Ride carefully, test the brakes at low speed first, then build up, and recheck for leaks, fluid levels and loose parts afterwards.
tasks.reason: The first ride is where small mistakes show up, while they're still cheap to fix.
tasks.expected: Ride notes recorded; nothing leaking or loose.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Ride notes recorded; nothing leaking or loose.

tasks.title: Set up the maintenance schedule
tasks.instructions: Open the Maintenance log, check each schedule item against your manual, and mark the services you just did so their next due dates start counting.
tasks.reason: The log can only tell you what's due once it knows when things were done.
tasks.expected: Every schedule item has a start point.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Every schedule item has a start point.

tasks.title: Back up the project
tasks.instructions: Download a backup from Settings.
tasks.reason: Your records are worth keeping somewhere safe.
tasks.expected: Backup file saved.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Backup file saved.

steps.acceptance: Both tires pass, or replacements ordered.

steps.title: Check the wheel bearings
steps.procedure: With each wheel off the ground, check for play and rough rotation, and replace bearings and seals if needed.
steps.acceptance: No play; smooth rotation; seals intact.

steps.title: Inspect the rims and wheels
steps.procedure: Check spoked wheels for loose or rusted spokes and runout, and cast wheels for cracks and bends.
steps.acceptance: Wheels true and sound, or sent to a wheel builder.

steps.title: Fit and balance new tires
steps.procedure: Fit new tires in the size, load and speed rating the manual or tire placard gives, with new valves or tubes, and balance the wheels.
steps.tools: Tire irons, balancer, or a shop
steps.acceptance: Correct tires fitted, beads seated, balanced, pressures set.

steps.title: Inspect the pads, shoes, discs and drums
steps.procedure: Check pad or shoe thickness and disc or drum condition on both brakes against the manual's limits.
steps.acceptance: Pads or shoes and discs or drums within limits, or replacements ordered.

steps.title: Rebuild or clean the calipers
steps.procedure: Strip and clean the calipers, check the pistons for pitting, replace the seals if they're sticky, and fit new pads.
steps.tools: Brake cleaner, caliper rebuild kits, torque wrench
steps.acceptance: Pistons move smoothly; new seals and pads fitted; bolts torqued.

steps.title: Service the master cylinders and hoses
steps.procedure: Rebuild sticky master cylinders and replace any brake hoses that are cracked, bulging or very old.
steps.acceptance: Master cylinders working; hoses sound or replaced.

steps.title: Bleed in fresh brake fluid
steps.procedure: Replace the brake fluid front and rear with the type on the reservoir cap, following the manual's order. On ABS bikes, follow the manual's ABS procedure.
steps.acceptance: Fresh fluid; firm lever and pedal; no leaks.

steps.title: Service the forks
steps.procedure: Replace the fork oil and seals, check the tubes for pitting and bends, and set the oil level from the manual.
steps.acceptance: Forks dry, oil at the right level, damping smooth.

steps.title: Check the steering head bearings
steps.procedure: With the front wheel off the ground, check for notchiness and play, and adjust, grease or replace the bearings.
steps.acceptance: Steering smooth with no play.

steps.title: Check the rear shocks and swingarm bearings
steps.procedure: Check the shock or shocks for leaks and damping, the swingarm pivot and any linkage for play, and grease the bearings.
steps.acceptance: Shocks dry and damping; no play at the pivot; bearings greased.

steps.title: Lube and adjust the control cables and levers
steps.procedure: Lube the throttle and other cables, check they're not frayed, set throttle play, and check the levers, pedals and footpegs.
steps.acceptance: Throttle snaps shut at both steering locks; cables lubed and adjusted; levers tight.

steps.title: Set the sag and suspension
steps.procedure: Measure the sag with you on the bike and set the preload and any damping adjusters for your weight and load.
steps.acceptance: Sag and settings recorded.

steps.workPackage: Reassemble, road test & keep it running
steps.title: Torque-check the critical fasteners
steps.procedure: Check the axles, pinch bolts, caliper bolts, handlebar clamps, engine mounts and drain plugs against the manual's torque values.
steps.acceptance: Each one checked, marked and initialed.

steps.workPackage: Reassemble, road test & keep it running
steps.title: Test ride and recheck
steps.procedure: Ride carefully, test the brakes at low speed first, then build up, and recheck for leaks, fluid levels and loose parts afterwards.
steps.acceptance: Ride notes recorded; nothing leaking or loose.

tasks.title: Check the CVT belt and variator
tasks.instructions: Remove the CVT cover, measure the belt width, inspect it for cracks and glazing, and check the variator rollers for flat spots.
tasks.reason: A worn belt slips and can snap; flat rollers make the scooter pull weakly.
tasks.expected: Belt width within the manual's limit; rollers round; case clean.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Belt width within the manual's limit; rollers round; case clean.

tasks.title: Check the clutch and bell
tasks.instructions: Inspect the clutch shoes for wear and the clutch bell for scoring, and check the torque spring.
tasks.reason: Worn shoes make the scooter judder or slip on take-off.
tasks.expected: Shoe thickness and bell within limits.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Shoe thickness and bell within limits.

tasks.title: Change the final gear oil
tasks.instructions: Drain and refill the final gear oil with the type and amount the manual gives.
tasks.reason: The final gear oil is small in volume and easy to forget.
tasks.expected: Fresh oil to the correct amount; plugs sealed.
tasks.inspectionCriteria: Fresh oil to the correct amount; plugs sealed.

steps.title: Test compression
steps.procedure: Do a compression test on every cylinder and compare the readings with the manual and with each other.
steps.acceptance: Readings for every cylinder recorded in Measurements.

steps.title: Start it and listen
steps.procedure: If the oil is good and the engine turns over freely, start it with fresh fuel and listen for knocks, rattles and rough running as it warms up.
steps.acceptance: Start-up behavior, noises and warning lights recorded, or why it wouldn't start.

steps.title: Change the oil and filter
steps.procedure: Drain the warm oil, replace the filter and drain bolt washer, and refill with the type and amount the manual gives.
steps.tools: Drain pan, filter wrench, torque wrench
steps.acceptance: New oil and filter; level correct; no leaks.

steps.title: Replace the spark plugs
steps.procedure: Replace the spark plugs with the type the manual lists, gapped to spec.
steps.tools: Plug socket, gap gauge, torque wrench
steps.acceptance: New plugs fitted, gapped and torqued.

steps.title: Check and adjust the valve clearances
steps.procedure: With the engine cold, measure every valve clearance and adjust any that are out of spec using the manual's method.
steps.acceptance: Every clearance recorded in Measurements and within spec.

steps.title: Service the cooling system
steps.procedure: Liquid-cooled: replace the coolant, check the radiator, hoses, cap and fan. Air-cooled: clean the fins and check any oil cooler and lines.
steps.acceptance: Coolant fresh and bled, or fins and oil cooler clean; fan works.

steps.title: Fix oil leaks and check the exhaust
steps.procedure: Find and fix oil leaks at covers and seals, and check the exhaust for leaks, rust-through and loose mounts.
steps.acceptance: No oil leaks; exhaust sealed and mounts tight.

steps.title: Check the CVT belt and variator
steps.procedure: Remove the CVT cover, measure the belt width, inspect it for cracks and glazing, and check the variator rollers for flat spots.
steps.acceptance: Belt width within the manual's limit; rollers round; case clean.

steps.title: Check the clutch and bell
steps.procedure: Inspect the clutch shoes for wear and the clutch bell for scoring, and check the torque spring.
steps.acceptance: Shoe thickness and bell within limits.

steps.title: Change the final gear oil
steps.procedure: Drain and refill the final gear oil with the type and amount the manual gives.
steps.acceptance: Fresh oil to the correct amount; plugs sealed.

steps.workPackage: Reassemble, road test & keep it running
steps.title: First start after the rebuild
steps.procedure: Prime the oil system if the manual says to, check for fuel leaks, start the engine and watch for leaks, smoke and warning lights.
steps.acceptance: Engine starts and idles; no fuel or oil leaks; warning lights normal.

steps.title: Drain and remove the fuel tank
steps.procedure: Drain the fuel into an approved can, disconnect the lines and any wiring, and remove the tank.
steps.acceptance: Tank off, drained and stored safely away from sparks.

steps.title: Find out which fuel system it has
steps.procedure: Check whether the bike has carburetors or fuel injection, and how many, and mark the steps below that don't apply as Cancelled.
steps.acceptance: Fuel system type noted; steps that don't apply cancelled.

steps.title: Clean the tank inside and check for rust
steps.procedure: Look inside the tank for rust, scale and old fuel varnish, clean it out, and seal it if there are pinholes.
steps.acceptance: Tank clean and dry inside; sealed if needed.

steps.title: Service the petcock or fuel pump, lines and filters
steps.procedure: Rebuild or replace the petcock, check the fuel pump if it has one, replace the fuel lines and filters, and check the tank vent.
steps.acceptance: New lines and filters; petcock or pump working; no leaks.

steps.title: Rebuild the carburetors
steps.procedure: Remove the carburetors, rebuild them one at a time with new gaskets, O-rings and needle valves, clean every passage, and set the float height.
steps.tools: Carb rebuild kits, carb cleaner, small screwdrivers
steps.acceptance: Carbs clean and rebuilt; float heights set to the manual's figure; jet sizes recorded.

steps.title: Check the fuel injection
steps.procedure: Read any fault codes, clean the throttle plates, check the injector wiring and fuel pressure as the manual describes.
steps.acceptance: No fault codes; throttle plates clean; idle steady.

steps.title: Air filter and intake boots
steps.procedure: Replace or clean the air filter and check the intake boots between the carbs or throttle bodies and the engine for cracks.
steps.acceptance: New or clean filter; intake boots sealed and crack-free.

steps.title: Synchronize the carbs or throttle bodies
steps.procedure: On multi-cylinder bikes, synchronize the carbs or throttle bodies with vacuum gauges, then set the idle.
steps.acceptance: Every cylinder balanced to the manual's figure; idle set.

steps.title: Test the vacuum fuel petcock
steps.procedure: Check the vacuum petcock opens only with vacuum and seals with the engine off, and replace its vacuum hose.
steps.acceptance: Petcock flows with vacuum and seals without; hose new.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the battery
steps.procedure: Disconnect the battery, negative first, and remove it for testing and charging.
steps.acceptance: Battery out and on a smart charger.

steps.title: Inspect the wiring harness and connectors
steps.procedure: Look over the harness for rubbed insulation, melted spots, old repairs and green corrosion in the connectors.
steps.acceptance: Harness checked; damage logged.

steps.title: Test and charge the battery
steps.procedure: Fully charge the battery and test it under load, or replace it if it's old or fails.
steps.acceptance: Battery passes, or a new one is fitted.

steps.title: Test the charging system
steps.procedure: With a good battery fitted, measure charging voltage at the battery and test the stator or alternator and the regulator using the manual's procedure.
steps.acceptance: Readings recorded and compared with the manual's figures.

steps.title: Clean the grounds, fuses and connectors
steps.procedure: Clean and tighten the main ground points, check every fuse and fuse holder, and clean the main connectors.
steps.tools: Contact cleaner, fine sandpaper, dielectric grease
steps.acceptance: Grounds clean and tight; fuses correct rating; connectors clean.

steps.title: Check the starter and ignition
steps.procedure: Check that the starter spins the engine strongly, and that every cylinder gets a good spark. On older bikes, check the points and condenser.
steps.acceptance: Starter and spark checked on every cylinder.

steps.title: Check lights, switches, horn and warning lamps
steps.procedure: Test every light, the horn, every switch and every warning lamp, and confirm the brake light works from both the front and rear brakes.
steps.acceptance: Every light and switch works; brake light works from lever and pedal.

steps.title: Short test ride, if it's safe
steps.procedure: If the brakes work, the tires hold air and the steering is free, ride slowly around the block and note how it brakes, shifts and handles.
steps.acceptance: Ride notes written, or ride skipped with the reason recorded.

steps.title: Inspect the frame and swingarm
steps.procedure: Inspect the frame, subframe, mounts and swingarm for cracks, bends, rust and crash damage.
steps.acceptance: Frame and swingarm checked; any damage logged.

steps.title: Check tire age, tread and damage
steps.procedure: Read the date code on both tires, measure the tread, and look for cracks, cuts, plugs and flat spots.
steps.acceptance: Both tires pass, or replacements ordered.

steps.title: Check the wheel bearings
steps.procedure: With each wheel off the ground, check for play and rough rotation, and replace bearings and seals if needed.
steps.acceptance: No play; smooth rotation; seals intact.

steps.title: Inspect the rims and wheels
steps.procedure: Check spoked wheels for loose or rusted spokes and runout, and cast wheels for cracks and bends.
steps.acceptance: Wheels true and sound, or sent to a wheel builder.

steps.title: Fit and balance new tires
steps.procedure: Fit new tires in the size, load and speed rating the manual or tire placard gives, with new valves or tubes, and balance the wheels.
steps.tools: Tire irons, balancer, or a shop
steps.acceptance: Correct tires fitted, beads seated, balanced, pressures set.

steps.procedure: Check pad or shoe thickness and disc or drum condition on both brakes against the manual's limits.
steps.acceptance: Pads or shoes and discs or drums within limits, or replacements ordered.

steps.title: Rebuild or clean the calipers

steps.tools: Brake cleaner, caliper rebuild kits, torque wrench
steps.acceptance: Pistons move smoothly; new seals and pads fitted; bolts torqued.

steps.title: Service the master cylinders and hoses
steps.procedure: Rebuild sticky master cylinders and replace any brake hoses that are cracked, bulging or very old.
steps.acceptance: Master cylinders working; hoses sound or replaced.

steps.title: Bleed in fresh brake fluid
steps.procedure: Replace the brake fluid front and rear with the type on the reservoir cap, following the manual's order. On ABS bikes, follow the manual's ABS procedure.
steps.acceptance: Fresh fluid; firm lever and pedal; no leaks.

steps.title: Service the forks
steps.procedure: Replace the fork oil and seals, check the tubes for pitting and bends, and set the oil level from the manual.
steps.acceptance: Forks dry, oil at the right level, damping smooth.

steps.title: Check the steering head bearings
steps.procedure: With the front wheel off the ground, check for notchiness and play, and adjust, grease or replace the bearings.
steps.acceptance: Steering smooth with no play.

steps.title: Check the rear shocks and swingarm bearings
steps.procedure: Check the shock or shocks for leaks and damping, the swingarm pivot and any linkage for play, and grease the bearings.
steps.acceptance: Shocks dry and damping; no play at the pivot; bearings greased.

steps.title: Lube and adjust the control cables and levers
steps.procedure: Lube the throttle and other cables, check they're not frayed, set throttle play, and check the levers, pedals and footpegs.
steps.acceptance: Throttle snaps shut at both steering locks; cables lubed and adjusted; levers tight.

steps.procedure: Measure the sag with you on the bike and set the preload and any damping adjusters for your weight and load.
